paper_metadata.title: The microstructural characteristics and mechanical properties of Nb-16Si-22Ti-2Al-2Cr alloys with Zr addition

evidence.quote: Compared with other high-temperature materials, the Nb-Si based alloys have become promising alternative materials because of their high melting points ( > 1750 ◦C), low density (~6.6 – 7.2 g/cm3) and excellent high-temperature strength.

These alloys were melted by the vacuum non-consumable arc furnace with tungsten electrode under a high-purity argon atmosphere in a water-cooled copper crucible.
Total weight of each prepared ingot was about 100 g, which was turned over and remelted six times to ensure compositional homogeneity.
Few Nb3Si phases are retained at room temperature because of the high cooling rate in water-cooled copper crucible.

Compared with KQ of 0Zr alloy (13.49 MPa m1/2), the fracture toughness increases when Zr content is up to 2 at.% (14.15 MPa m1/2), and then drops with the increase in the Zr content from 4 to 8 at.%.
Noticeably, the fracture toughness abnormally increases to 14.03 MPa m1/2 when the content of added Zr is up to 10 at.%.

The elastic modulus of α -Nb5Si3 is 309.2 GPa for the 0Zr alloy, which is near to the elastic modulus value of α -Nb5Si3 (327 GPa) reported by Kim [33] but lower than the result (355 GPa) reported by Sankar [23].
